summary: RL training method for SWE agents that converts runtime signals into step-level rewards: a navigation potential (how many gold-patch files the agent has inspected) and a verification potential (how many fail-to-pass tests are fixed without breaking pass-to-pass tests), measured by replaying edits in a parallel 'shadow' sandbox. Trained Qwen3.5-9B (issue repair) and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (repo generation) and reports gains over GRPO and four process-reward baselines.

claims.claim: SWE-MILE improves issue resolution over outcome-only and other process-reward RL methods.
claims.evidence: Table 2: Avg@4 SWE-bench Verified 63.8 vs base 53.6, GRPO 58.2, best baseline SWE-TRACE 60.5; SWE-bench Pro 39.3 vs base 30.8, GRPO 33.9, SWE-TRACE 36.6. Avg@4 gives some sampling averaging but no per-seed training variance; checkpoint is the best one evaluated every five steps, apparently on the test benchmarks (App. B.1).

claims.claim: Improves whole-repository generation with fewer turns and shorter responses.
claims.evidence: Table 3: Doc2Repo 54.7 vs GRPO 51.3 / GraphGPO 52.4; NL2Repo-Bench 33.1 vs SWE-TRACE 30.9; turns 72.6 vs 85.7-112.0 on Doc2Repo. Doc2Repo has only 50 tasks.

claims.claim: Both potentials, backward credit and RLOO advantage each contribute; structured tools beat bash-only.
claims.evidence: Table 4: w/o milestone 59.4/34.7, w/o verification 60.7/35.8, w/o navigation 62.0/38.0, Bash only 62.2/38.6 vs full 63.8/39.3 (Verified/Pro). Several ablation deltas are 1-2 pp without variance.

claims.claim: Asynchronous shadow probing hides most verification latency.
claims.evidence: §2.6 reports runtime overhead over 9,600 rollouts with a tail-latency breakdown; only measured on the authors' SWE-MiniSandbox setup.

patterns.note: RL with runtime-derived process rewards outperforms outcome-only GRPO by ~5.6 pp on SWE-bench Verified and ~5.4 pp on SWE-bench Pro for a 9B model.
Intermediate test execution (F2P/P2P states after each edit) is the strongest training signal; removing verification potential costs more than removing navigation.
Bash-only action space slightly underperforms structured search/read/edit tools (62.2 vs 63.8 Verified).
Namespace/cgroup sandboxes (primary + shadow) for replay and verification.

methodology.sample: Train: 1,952 Python SWE-rebench V2 tasks; 3,675 DeNovoSWE tasks. Test: SWE-bench Verified 500, SWE-bench Pro public 731, NL2Repo-Bench 104, Doc2Repo 50.
methodology.baselines: GRPO, G-RA, SWE-TRACE (reimplemented, no official code; judge swapped to Qwen3.8-27B), GiGPO, GraphGPO, DeNovoSWE-Agent; same data/budgets. Proprietary model numbers listed for context only.
methodology.models: Qwen3.5-9B (issue resolution), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (repo generation); one policy per task type.
methodology.variance: Avg@4 inference sampling; no repeated training runs, no CIs; best checkpoint selection every five steps.
methodology.ablations: Component removal, advantage estimator, bash-only, potential-weight sensitivity (Fig. 3).
methodology.contamination_controls: None reported for SWE-rebench training vs SWE-bench Verified/Pro test overlap.
methodology.languages: Training Python-only for issue resolution; SWE-bench Pro includes JS/TS/Go at test; limitations note per-language test parsing pipelines are required.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint (23 pages); no venue listed.
standards.artifacts: Code at https://github.com/CcQunResearch/SWE-MILE; prompts in App. E; hyperparameters in Tables 5-6.

biases.detail: Best checkpoint chosen among periodic evaluations without a stated separate validation split, so reported Avg@4 may be optimistically selected on test benchmarks.
Single training run per method; ablation deltas of 1-2 pp are uninterpretable without seeds.
Issue-resolution training data is the Python subset; verification potential needs per-language test parsers (D.2).
SWE-TRACE was reimplemented from the paper with a substituted judge model; fidelity to the original is unverified.
No decontamination between SWE-rebench training tasks and SWE-bench evaluation reported.

coi.affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / UCAS; Tencent Inc. (3 of 5 authors).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None of Tencent's products; Qwen base models.
coi.detail: Vendor-affiliated authors evaluating their own training method, not a commercial product.

verdict_reason: Abstract claims are backed by Tables 2-4 with numbers that match, code is released, and baselines are recent; but it is a single-run, test-set-checkpoint-selected RL result on Python-trained small models, and is about model training rather than harness configuration.
applicability: Low direct relevance: a Java team adopting hosted agents will not run RLVR training. Two indirect lessons transfer: (1) running tests after each repository-changing edit is the most valuable progress signal, which argues for a harness hook that runs the affected module's JUnit/contract tests on every edit across the ≥4 ingestion repos, not only at the end; (2) structured read/edit/search tools modestly beat raw bash. The shadow-sandbox replay idea could inform asynchronous CI-style verification in a harness, but the paper only shows it for training throughput. Nothing on specs, Java build systems, or mixed hosts.
